transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-16 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Nimbus Head of ML), Amira Khan (Infra), Liam O'Neill (Product)

Summary: quick recap of last week's runs, went over numbers, talked about pinning to rwd-7b-q8 (voice: mis-typed product names possible), discussed fallback to hosted smaller model for cost spikes, and next steps on security and canary rollout.

[00:00] Jordan: alright good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, um we'll take about 45, ish minutes, mainly bench reviews and then model selection, sound good?
[00:08] Carlos: yep that works for us, thanks Jordan
[00:12] Maya: hey everyone, just to note I updated the run IDs in the spreadsheet, there's a new column for prefix cache on/off, sorry kv cache, um the numbers changed a bit
[00:24] Liam: cool thanks Maya
[00:30] Jordan: okay first slide, overview — latency median and p99 from last week's run on your sample customer queries, average seq length around 280 tokens, yeah we saw median of 120 ms on the rwd-7b-q8 pinned to dedicated pool and p99 around 420 ms
[00:52] Carlos: 420 p99 is ok, but we care about the tail, we're doing interactive chat in-store kiosks so 400+ is kinda noticeable
[01:05] Maya: right, when we enabled prefix (kv) caching the p99 dropped to 310 on the same model, so that was a meaningful win — though warms up matters, we saw cold starts still hit 800+
[01:22] Amira: are those cold start numbers for the dedicated or hosted?
[01:25] Maya: dedicated GPU pool — cold start due to model load time, that's where burst capacity helps; also quantized models load faster but still non-zero
[01:36] Jordan: and cost rundown: per-1M tokens the q8 pinned dedicated run was roughly 40% cheaper than using the hosted non-quantized larger model, but if you over-provision for latency the unit cost creeps up
[01:50] Carlos: hmm ok so cost/latency tradeoff — we might prefer predictability even if slightly higher median latency
[01:58] Jordan: totally, that's why pinning is attractive, you get predictable throughput and isolation, but you lose some of Redwood's automatic fallback unless you add explicit fallback routes
[02:12] Liam: can you clarify fallback? like if dedicated pool is saturated what happens?
[02:17] Maya: default is we queue or autoscale per your policy; for POC we recommend an explicit fallback to a hosted smaller variant, e.g., rwd-3b-fp16-hosted, so in periods of high load you still respond albeit with different quality/cost profile
[02:33] Carlos: and how automatic is that? Do we have to change code?
[02:36] Jordan: you configure routing policy in the Console, canary + fallback are declarative. We can demo it but it doesn't need app code changes; it's a routing layer thing
[02:47] Amira: ok on security — we've started the SOC2 docs pull, can you send the SOC2 snapshot and the list of audit logs available?
[02:55] Jordan: yes I'll send the SOC2 link and a doc that lists audit log retention and export patterns. Also note KMS integrations for private deployments, that requires some setup on your side
[03:06] Amira: noted, we'll need KMS policy names and the timeline for VPC peering
[03:12] Maya: I'll follow up with the VPC peering checklist and sample CF/Terraform snippets; for peering we usually ask for a maintenance window for initial handshake
[03:20] Carlos: back to models — we did evals on relevance on 200 prompts, rwd-7b-q8 had a tiny drop in BLEU-style numbers vs the fp16 baseline but human eval showed parity on the most common intents
[03:35] Liam: that's promising, does the q8 suffer on longer context? we have multi-turn dialogs sometimes 10+ turns
[03:41] Maya: quantization can sometimes cause more hallucination on edge cases, longer context memory a little noisier; we recommend extensive eval on your specific prompt set and then pin with small canary rollouts
[03:54] Carlos: what about rollbacks? if pinned model performs worse in canary what are our options?
[03:58] Jordan: you can rollback to previous pinned version via the Console; we've built rollback hooks so traffic is shifted back and we keep traces for debugging. We also support an instantaneous fallback route to a hosted variant while rollback completes
[04:12] Liam: how long does a rollback take?
[04:15] Maya: depends on warm caches and model load; with pre-warmed replicas it's a few seconds to a minute for routing change, but if model needs to be loaded cold it could be 2-5 minutes for initial requests to stabilize
[04:30] Carlos: that's fine as long as user experience is acceptable. We need to define SLOs for the POC, like p99 < 500 ms and availability 99.9% for core flows
[04:42] Jordan: noted, we'll capture those in the success criteria doc
[04:46] Liam: one more on benchmarking — can you show the spreadsheet?
[04:50] Jordan: yes shared in chat: https://shared.redwood/reports/nimbus-poc-benchmarks (note: placeholder link) — the runs are labeled run-20260609-*
[05:02] Maya: looking at the runs, run-07 with kv-cache on looks best; run-03 had weird throughput dips, might've been infra throttling when we hit the burst limit
[05:15] Amira: what causes infra throttling? is that our VPC or Redwood side?
[05:19] Maya: usually queueing or hitting concurrency limits in the dedicated pool; we can increase pool size or allow burst to hosted, both config changes in Dedicated settings
[05:30] Carlos: for cost modeling, what's the differential if we enable burst to hosted vs reserve higher dedicated?
[05:36] Jordan: if you enable burst the unit cost per token can spike because hosted rates are higher, but you avoid over-commitment. We'll put a scenario table in the spreadsheet — I'll add a column for burst-on vs fixed-capacity cost projections
[05:49] Liam: about canary rollouts — do we do traffic percentage routing? like 5% to canary?
[05:54] Maya: yes, Console allows percentage based rollouts, and automatic rollback if quality metrics dropped. For POC we recommend starting at 5% for 1 hour then 20% for 24 hours, then full if stable
[06:07] Carlos: what are quality metrics for auto-rollback? can we use our own metric?
[06:11] Jordan: you can plug in custom metrics via the tracing hook or send batch eval results; we also support golden-set checks where we run a small eval set continuously
[06:21] Amira: KMS question again — for private deployment do you support customer-managed key in HSM?
[06:27] Maya: yes, KMS/HSM integrations supported for Private; for Dedicated you'll typically use Redwood-managed KMS unless you opt for Private or a hybrid with BYOK
[06:36] Carlos: timeline — we'd like to move to canary in your staging infra by June 24th, is that feasible?
[06:41] Jordan: yes if we have VPC peering and SOC artifacts this week; action items to get those from your side, Redwood will prep canary config and test harness
[06:50] Liam: one weird hiccup we saw — a couple of responses were truncated mid-sentence in run-05, any idea?
[06:56] Maya: that might be due to our tokenization/streaming boundary; could be client-side stream handling too, we'll repro with streaming on and off
[07:05] Jordan: ok we'll repro and log it as a bug if it persists
[07:08] Carlos: anything else on model selection? I'm leaning to pin rwd-7b-q8 for canary with fallback to rwd-3b-hosted
[07:17] Liam: agreed, gives us cost predictability and a safety net
[07:20] Amira: agree but we need a clear rollback playbook and the SSO + audit log access before production
[07:26] Jordan: understood, we'll draft the rollback playbook and send SOC2 / audit log doc. Also include Terraform snippets for VPC peering
[07:36] Maya: I'll run the additional p99/99.9 profiles and attach them to the spreadsheet; also include a warmup script for reducing cold starts
[07:45] Jordan: perfect — any final questions?
[07:48] Carlos: none from me, thanks everyone
[07:50] Liam: no, thanks
[07:51] Amira: all good
[07:52] Jordan: great we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the canary for the week of 6/22 — sending notes after this call

Recap / Next steps (verbal): Jordan to share benchmark spreadsheet + cost scenarios, Maya to run additional latency tests with kv/prefix caching and warmup script, Amira to provide VPC peering window and KMS contact, Carlos to confirm acceptance criteria for accuracy and SLOs.

Links shared in chat: https://shared.redwood/reports/nimbus-poc-benchmarks (benchmarks), https://shared.redwood/docs/soc2 (SOC2 placeholder), link to VPC peering checklist (placeholder)

End of transcript.
